scenes.narration: Voice and video can't wait in a queue. Email can wait quite happily. Q o S decides who goes first.

scenes.heading: The VIP security lane
scenes.narration: Think of an airport with a fast lane for VIPs. Classification spots which packets are which. Marking stamps them with a priority value, called D S C P. Voice gets E F, which is forty six. L L Q gives voice a strict priority queue.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. It doesn't create bandwidth. Priority is limited. C o S doesn't cross routers.

items.right: It only chooses who goes first

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Classify, mark, then queue. Voice is E F, forty six. Q o S can't create bandwidth. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva QoS lab.
